name: scan-write-lock-on-the-fast-path
body:
`cmd_scan` holds the per-checkout extended write lock (`artifacts::acquire_spec_lock`, a blocking `LOCK_EX` flock on `apg/.trans/specs.lock`) for the whole scan pipeline, including the freshness fast path where the tree is unchanged and the DB is reused with no frontend spawn and no rebuild — a read-only scan of an unchanged tree still takes an exclusive lock and can briefly block a staleness-gated reader. That is deliberate: the reuse decision and the rebuild stay under one lock, so a reader never judges a half-decided state. The same lock covers the previous-database read: after the fast-path return, `cmd_scan` takes exactly one read-only `PreviousScan::capture` before the pipeline discards or replaces `db.lbug`; the handle is released inside `capture`, so the rebuild replaces the database uncontended and no consumer opens a second handle on it. Upgrade trigger: if the fast path's brief exclusivity ever measurably delays a concurrent reader, acquire a shared (`LOCK_SH`) lock for the reusable branch only — do not weaken the exclusive hold on the discard-and-rebuild path or move the capture outside the lock. On the delta route `cmd_scan` skips the `warm::reuse_universe` union whenever `incremental::reuse_universe_needed` returns false (the captured local seed's `content_key` equals the recorded key and every reused file with a recorded unit is a File in `previous.scanned`), with the fact-store index loaded lazily; an empty or unreadable index makes every reused file count as having a recorded unit, so each one is checked against `previous.scanned` and the union runs only if some reused file is missing from the local database. A skipped union also skips the module scaffolding `reuse_universe` would add for languages the delta run does not re-target, which rests on the local seed already holding it at the same content key. Upgrade trigger: if a false spec drift ever names a skipped language's module after a delta scan, add that scaffolding check to `reuse_universe_needed` (or keep the union for languages with no re-targeted file).

The scan intent is cleared only on the post-record success path — an errored scan (pipeline or layers-ingest failure) leaves it to `INTENT_GRACE_SECS` (15 min), so a read/reuse phase longer than that window is unprotected — and the intent write opens one extra write transaction (re-taking `facts.lock`) at the start of every non-fast-path scan, so store contention now fails the scan before prepare/frontends rather than after the frontend work (deliberate fail-fast, matching the probe and the phase-3 record boundary). Upgrade trigger: add a drop-guard when the read/reuse phase could exceed the grace window, or fold the intent write into an existing write transaction if the extra lock acquisition becomes a measured cost.
